problem_statement: When CONFIG_EVENTS is enabled, an application using the event APIs can trigger a debug assertion failure in the kernel. The situation can occur after nxevent_post() sets bits on an nxevent_t object, followed by nxevent_clear() clearing selected bits and a subsequent nxevent_wait() or nxevent_trywait() call using NXEVENT_WAIT_NOCLEAR. If another thread posts the same event while a thread is in nxevent_wait() or nxevent_trywait(), the wait operation can complete, but the kernel can then fail a debug assertion in the event-wait implementation and the process can exit with a non-zero status. The observable defect is that nxevent_wait() and nxevent_trywait() do not always complete normally under concurrent event posting, and the behavior can also expose incorrect visibility of cleared bits. The required behavior is that posting events must not cause waiting callers to abort with an assertion; nxevent_wait() and nxevent_trywait() must complete normally and return the currently available event bits; with NXEVENT_WAIT_NOCLEAR they must not clear event bits; nxevent_clear() must clear only the bits specified in its argument; and bits cleared by nxevent_clear() must not be returned by later nxevent_wait() or nxevent_trywait() calls.

superseded_statements.problem_statement: With CONFIG_SCHED_EVENTS enabled, running the new nxevent clear/trywait test cases triggers an assertion failure in the kernel nxevent wait path (event_wait.c) because nxevent_post leaves a waiter node in an inconsistent state; the test expects nxevent_clear and nxevent_wait/trywait with NXEVENT_WAIT_NOCLEAR to behave correctly without hitting that assertion.
check_issues: `problem_statement` gives the fix away: "nxevent_post leaves a waiter node in an inconsistent state". Describe only the observable symptom, its trigger and the required behavior, not what the code checks or must do internally

superseded_statements.problem_statement: On a NuttX configuration with event support enabled, such as a2g-tc397-5v-tft with events enabled, testing/ostest fails when nxevent_test includes the added clear cases. The added section posts 0xff to the event with NXEVENT_POST_SET and then exercises nxevent_clear() together with NXEVENT_WAIT_NOCLEAR: clear 0 followed by wait and trywait for 0xf; clear 0xf followed by trywait for 0xf; clear 0 followed by wait and trywait for 0xf0; and clear 0xf0 followed by trywait for 0xf0. The expected results are 0xf, 0, 0xf0, and 0, respectively. Before the kernel fix, running ostest aborts with a kernel assertion failure during the event test and the process exits with a nonzero status instead of reporting nxevent_test as passed. The observed failure is an assertion failure rather than a simple wrong return value from the added NXEVENT_TEST cases. The issue is triggered by the normal interaction of posting, clearing, and waiting on the same event in this test. The required behavior is that the kernel handles these event operations consistently so nxevent_test completes and the added cases produce the expected return values without an assertion failure.

verification.reason: The statement covers the clear behavior, but its return-value description is ambiguous about whether nxevent_wait/nxevent_trywait return all set bits or only the requested bits. This can be repaired by clarifying the public return semantics without describing the implementation.

problems.detail: The statement says nxevent_wait()/nxevent_trywait() return “the currently available event bits,” which is ambiguous between all bits currently set in the event and only the bits matching the requested mask. The hidden tests require only the requested mask’s available bits (e.g. 0xf when 0xff is set, and 0 when the requested bits were cleared).
The exact returned values 0, 0xf, and 0xf0 for masked waits are not fully specified unless “available event bits” is interpreted relative to the requested mask.

problem_statement_fixed: When CONFIG_EVENTS is enabled, an application using the event APIs can trigger a debug assertion failure in the kernel. The situation can occur after nxevent_post() sets bits on an nxevent_t object, followed by nxevent_clear() clearing selected bits and a subsequent nxevent_wait() or nxevent_trywait() call using NXEVENT_WAIT_NOCLEAR. If another thread posts the same event while a thread is in nxevent_wait() or nxevent_trywait(), the wait operation can complete, but the kernel can then fail a debug assertion in the event-wait implementation and the process can exit with a non-zero status. The observable defect is that nxevent_wait() and nxevent_trywait() do not always complete normally under concurrent event posting, and the behavior can also expose incorrect visibility of cleared bits. The required behavior is that posting events must not cause waiting callers to abort with an assertion; nxevent_wait() and nxevent_trywait() must complete normally and return only the bits of the requested event mask that are currently available (that is, the intersection of the mask passed to the call and the bits currently set in the event; if none of the requested bits are available, 0 is returned); with NXEVENT_WAIT_NOCLEAR they must not clear event bits; nxevent_clear() must clear only the bits specified in its argument, including leaving all bits set when the argument is 0; and bits cleared by nxevent_clear() must not be returned by later nxevent_wait() or nxevent_trywait() calls.
